item.title: New farming equipment for Tonga's organic farmers
item.description: Seventy-eight organic farmers across Tonga have received essential farming equipment to help strengthen agroecological and organic farming practices. The distribution coordinated by the Pacific Community ( SPC ), went to farmers on Tonga's two main island groups: Tongatapu and Vava'u.
item.content:encoded:
Seventy-eight organic farmers across Tonga have received essential farming equipment to help strengthen agroecological and organic farming practices.

The distribution coordinated by the Pacific Community ( SPC ), went to farmers on Tonga's two main island groups: Tongatapu and Vava'u.

The support is part of the Pacific Organic Learning Farms Network ( POLFN ) project's commitment to improving farmers' access to appropriate tools and technologies that enhance productivity, resilience, and sustainable agricultural practices.

Farmers received a range of equipment, including machetes, soil augers, drip irrigation systems, chainsaws, and weed eaters, to support their day-to-day farming activities.

Farmer and Women’s group leader, Melesila Weilert, Tongatapu, shared that the support comes at a crucial time for their community, where many residents have left to participate in seasonal work programmes in Australia and New Zealand.

“With a population of around 226 people in our village, many have joined the seasonal worker programmes overseas. Those of us who remain and are still able to do the physical work are mostly women,” she said.

“As mothers, we know that we also have a responsibility to help provide for our children and support our families’ day-to-day livelihoods. Opportunities like this will help us step up, strengthen our farming activities, and do what we can to improve the wellbeing of our households.”

While many farmers are often tempted to rely on pesticides and herbicides for convenience, access to appropriate farming tools provides practical alternatives that support organic production methods.

POLFN Farm Advisor, Amanaki Funaki, said the equipment distribution would help farmers adopt agroecological practices more effectively while reducing their dependence on chemical inputs.

" These tools are an investment in our farmers and in the future of organic agriculture in Tonga.” Amanaki said.

POLFN Project Implementation Officer, Emosi Cagi, said the distribution reflects the project's commitment to equipping farmers with the resources they need to put their training into practice.

" Through the Pacific Organic Learning Farms Network, we want to ensure they have access to the tools needed to apply agroecological practices on their farms. When farmers have both the skills and the right equipment, they are better positioned to improve their livelihoods while contributing to more sustainable and climate-resilient food systems." Cagi said.

In Vava'u, organic farmer and bishop David Lolohea believes the support will have an impact far beyond his own farm.

" As both a farmer and a church leader, I hope this support will inspire others in our community to embrace organic farming. I want to encourage more farmers to become part of this movement. By working together and sharing our experiences, we can strengthen organic farming across Vava'u and leave behind healthier land for our children.”

The equipment distribution forms part of the Pacific Organic Learning Farms Network's ongoing efforts to strengthen agroecological farming across Tonga through farmer training, peer-to-peer learning, demonstration farms, and access to appropriate farming technologies.

This work is part of the Pacific Organic Learning Farms ( POLFN ) Project under the KIWA Initiative, managed by the POETC om initiative at SPC . The KIWA initiative is funded by the European Union, Agence Françe de Développement ( AFD ), Global Affairs Canada ( GAC ), Australia's Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade ( DFAT ) and New Zealand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade ( MFAT ).

item.title: Int'l Humanitarian Day highlights community-led disaster preparedness

item.content:encoded:
The Tonga Family Health Association ( TFHA ) has marked International Humanitarian Day in Nuku'alofa today with a focus on strengthening community resilience and ensuring humanitarian action upholds justice, dignity and equity.

TFHA executive director, Pelenatita Longopa, said the day called attention to the rising threats and attacks against aid workers and civilians, while calling for an end to impunity for violations of international humanitarian law.

Through its SPRINT IV Project, TFHA has positioned sexual and reproductive health ( SRH ) as a critical humanitarian priority, particularly during disasters when essential services can be disrupted or overlooked.

TFHA 's humanitarian work includes providing women, girls and vulnerable groups with access to mental health care, contraception and protection from gender-based violence.

Pelenatita Longopa said SRH was central to resilience because it protected the health and dignity of families during crises, empowered women and young people to participate in recovery and strengthened coordination between health, protection and communities.

Community representatives and humanitarians said humanitarian preparedness was a lived reality for Tonga, with the country's experience of volcanic eruptions and cyclones demonstrating the need for community-driven resilience.

The Civil Society Forum of Tonga also received donated humanitarian supplies from UN Global Medics, including hygiene packs and a water purifier intended to support families during future disasters.

The second half of the event featured a roundtable discussion involving humanitarian workers, volunteers, non-government organisations representatives and community members.

Discussions focused on how communities experienced and remembered the 2022 Hunga Tonga-Hunga Ha'apai volcanic eruption, including humanitarian challenges faced during the response.

Participants also examined lessons from the response, including what worked well, gaps in humanitarian coordination and challenges faced by agencies and communities.

The discussion also looked at the way forward, including how communities and service providers could strengthen disaster preparedness and resilience through strategic planning.

item.title: Push on for Talatau Amone to come back in World Cup
item.description: Talatau Amone could be cleared to return for Tonga in the World Cup, with the exiled half in a grey area while banned from the NRL and playing Queensland Cup. Talatau Amone could be given the chance to press his case for an NRL return on the World Cup stage, with talks under way to see if the former St George Illawarra half can be cleared to play for Tonga.
item.content:encoded:
Talatau Amone could be cleared to return for Tonga in the World Cup, with the exiled half in a grey area while banned from the NRL and playing Queensland Cup.

Talatau Amone could be given the chance to press his case for an NRL return on the World Cup stage, with talks under way to see if the former St George Illawarra half can be cleared to play for Tonga.

AAP understands International Rugby League officials have reached out to the NRL to query Amone's availability, following his impressive return in the Queensland Cup.

Tonga have also made inquiries and are monitoring the situation closely, with the 24-year-old every chance of being part of their plans if cleared.

Amone last played NRL for St George Illawarra in 2023, before being deregistered following a conviction for an assault involving a hammer.

He was ordered to serve an intensive correction order in the community, bringing a halt to his 51-game NRL career.

But Amone has now scored three tries and set up eight in five games for Wynnum-Manly in the Queensland Cup.

That form has prompted one NRL club official to privately declare Amone would walk straight into a No.6 jersey, after he set up four tries and six line-breaks in his first game alone.

Tonga have also watched his form closely, after the former Dragon was part of their most recent World Cup squad in 2022.

The Queensland Rugby League liaised with the NRL 's integrity unit before clearing his Wynnum-Manly return, with Amone allowed to play in State Cup competitions.

But AAP understands Amone remains precluded from holding an NRL contract until at least February, when a community corrections order for a separate matter ends.

The half is also working through programs with Wynnum-Manly, as he attempts to get his career back on track.

The ARL Commission is effectively organising this year's World Cup, prompting IRL chair Troy Grant to reach out to ARLC counterpart Peter V'landys to seek clarity on Amone's status.

Legal advice is being sought on the matter, with an outcome expected shortly. All parties are working towards Amone playing in the tournament.

Players need not hold an NRL contract to play in the event, but Amone's current restrictions have created a grey area.

Tonga coach Kristian Woolf used a makeshift five-eighth in Isaiah Iongi next to Dolphins star Isaiya Katoa in last year's Pacific Cup.

Former Warriors and Wests Tigers livewire Tuimoala Lolohea is another option from the Super League, having last played for Tonga in 2024.

But Tonga have kept a close watch on Amone's strong early form for Wynnum-Manly, and he is believed to be in consideration.

A recognised five-eighth would serve Tonga well in the tournament, given they possess one of the game's most damaging forward packs, can strike out wide and the ever-improving Katoa at halfback.

Selection would also act as a massive boost for Amone, who is keen to return to the NRL after not playing on the big stage for more than three years.

Amone last played Tests for Tonga as a 20-year-old in the 2022 World Cup, where an inexperienced Katoa and Lolohea played in the halves.
